messages:
jonathan: heads-up — deploybot kicked off kernel rollout to prod: `kernel=v3.7.2-quant-abel`, canary=night-bucket (2%). starting now.
deploy-bot: Rollout started · kernel=v3.7.2-quant-abel · canary=night-bucket · id=rb-2025-03-15-01
maria: seeing p99 jump in the canary within 6 mins, from ~220ms -> ~1.8s, and a handful of 502s. linking the dashboard: https://dash.redwood/pc/abc123
sre-oncall: pause the rollout. please pin traffic back to `kernel=v3.7.1` for night-bucket and halt further shards. i'll investigate traces.
sim: ack. running deploybot command: `deploybot pin --kernel v3.7.1 --scope night-bucket --ttl 2h` — doing a dry-run then apply.
chad: fwiw i saw similar on staging yesterday but only for `quant-abel` when running small-batch lanes (<8 tokens). suspect a quant codepath hit that regresses micro-batching perf.
build-bot: automatic build validation: quant-abel vs quant-abel-legacy

```
[2025-03-15T01:06:22Z] x86_64-cuda: ABI mismatch detected in qconv_kern.cu: symbol hash != expected
[2025-03-15T01:06:22Z] fallback: some kernels loaded from host lib, performance penalty observed
```

maria: exact log we saw on canary node (trimmed):
```
W infer/runtime: kv-cache cache miss spike
E runtime: kernel qconv init mismatch -> 502
latency p99 1.8s
```

jonathan: if it's ABI mismatch + fallback kernels that explains spike. does that mean a bad quant build landed into the kernel bundle? who owns the quant build pipeline now?
chad: looks like `quant-abel` artifact was rebuilt with a different toolchain; kernel ABI bumped. runtime still tries to load optimized kernels but falls back to slower generic path. reproduction on local GPU identical.
ashley: from product side — we need a short release-note blurb and customer-facing status. propose: "Rolling update paused after canary observed latency regressions for small-batch traffic; rolling back to prior kernel while we rebuild compatible quant kernels." Thoughts?
sre-oncall: agree. customer-facing should avoid deep technical details. internal release note should include repro steps and blame chain.
sim: rollout is paused and night-bucket pinned to `v3.7.1`. deploybot returned:
```
Pinned kernel v3.7.1 for scope night-bucket until 2025-03-15T03:10Z (2h)
Rollout suspended for remaining shards
```
jonathan: ops action items:
- sim: keep pin in place until quant rebuild validated on canaries
- chad + build-bot: produce a rollback-friendly quant artifact (tag `quant-abel@v3.7.1-compat`) and run full matrix
- maria + sre-oncall: smoke canary once artifact available, watch p99, 5xx rate, and kernel load logs
- ashley: draft external blurb + internal postmortem placeholder
chad: i'll kick a rebuild now with the pinned toolchain and add a CI gate for ABI hash. ETA ~45m for first artifacts.
build-bot: started rebuild job id=bb-8843, matrix: [cuda12.1, cuda11.8] · will publish s3://redwood-builds/quant-abel/compat/
maria: once build finishes i'll run quick canary deployment to night-bucket (0.5% -> 2%) and report p95/p99 within 10m.
ashley: external blurb (draft): "We paused a rolling update after we detected a latency regression in a small subset of traffic. We've reverted the canary and are rebuilding a compatible inference artifact; we'll follow up with a postmortem. No customer data was impacted." ok? :eyes:
sre-oncall: fine. add a pointer to status page and ETA to follow-up. keep the ol' `incident` tag for internal traceability.
jonathan: thanks all. i'll hold any further kernel rollouts until we sign off on the new quant-abel artifact. update this thread with build id and canary smoke results. :thumbsup:
